description: Protected characteristics and prohibited interview topics used by the Step 1 compliance scrub. Inlined into the analyst prompt at build time. Federal entries apply everywhere in the US; state entries are gated on config/company-profile.json -> jurisdiction.state. This is an engineering default, NOT legal advice — have counsel review before production use, and see docs/COMPLIANCE.md.

categories.label: Race / Color
unacceptable: Any question about race, color, or ethnicity
Questions about hair texture or protective hairstyles (CROWN Act states)
acceptable: Voluntary, anonymous EEO self-identification collected separately from the hiring process

categories.label: National Origin / Citizenship
unacceptable: Where are you from originally?
What is your first language?
Are you a US citizen?
Questions about accent, ancestry, or birthplace
acceptable: Are you authorized to work in the country where this role is based?
Will you now or in the future require sponsorship?
categories.note: Export-control roles may lawfully ask a narrowly-scoped 'US person' status question where a specific regime genuinely applies. That is a legal-status question, not a national-origin question, and must be scripted by counsel. See docs/COMPLIANCE.md.

categories.label: Religion
unacceptable: What religion do you practice?
Do you observe any religious holidays?
What church do you attend?
acceptable: This role requires occasional weekend coverage — can you meet that schedule?

categories.label: Sex / Gender Identity / Sexual Orientation
unacceptable: Questions about gender identity, transition status, sexual orientation, or pronouns as an eligibility matter
acceptable: Nothing role-relevant turns on this category

categories.label: Pregnancy / Marital & Family Status
unacceptable: Are you married?
Do you have children?
Are you planning to start a family?
What does your spouse do?
Who watches your kids?
acceptable: This role requires travel roughly one week per month — can you meet that requirement?

categories.label: Age
unacceptable: How old are you?
When did you graduate high school?
When do you plan to retire?
Digital native / recent grad framing
acceptable: Do you meet the minimum experience requirement for this role?

categories.label: Disability / Medical
unacceptable: Do you have any disabilities?
Have you filed a workers' compensation claim?
How many sick days did you take?
Any questions about family medical history
acceptable: Can you perform the essential functions of this role, with or without reasonable accommodation?

categories.label: Salary History
unacceptable: What do you currently make?
What was your last base salary?
What is your current total comp?
acceptable: What are your compensation expectations for this role?
Here is the posted range for this role — does that work for you?
categories.note: Banned in a growing number of states and cities. company-profile.jurisdiction.salary_history_ban gates enforcement; leave it true unless counsel says otherwise.

categories.label: Arrest & Conviction Record
unacceptable: Have you ever been arrested?
Any criminal-history question before a conditional offer in ban-the-box jurisdictions
acceptable: Post-offer, job-related conviction screening conducted under the applicable statute with individualized assessment

categories.label: Military / Veteran Status
unacceptable: What type of discharge did you receive?
Are you in the reserves and could you be deployed?

categories.label: Credit History / Financial Status
unacceptable: Do you own or rent?
Have you ever declared bankruptcy?
Have your wages been garnished?
acceptable: Post-offer, role-justified credit screening with FCRA disclosure and authorization

categories.label: Genetic Information
unacceptable: Any question about family medical history or genetic testing

adds: FEHA protections exceed federal coverage and reach employers with 5+ employees.
Salary history inquiry is prohibited outright, and the pay scale must be provided on reasonable request.
Criminal-history inquiry is barred until after a conditional offer.
Protective hairstyles are protected under the CROWN Act.
Protected categories additionally include medical condition, genetic information, and military/veteran status.
Salary history inquiry is prohibited statewide.
NYC requires a bias audit and candidate notice for automated employment decision tools.
Caregiver status is a protected category in NYC.
Candidates must be notified when AI is used to analyze video interviews, with consent obtained.

framework: Colorado Equal Pay for Equal Work Act
adds: Compensation range and benefits must be disclosed in the job posting.

framework: Washington Equal Pay and Opportunities Act
adds: Salary range must be disclosed in the posting for employers with 15+ employees.

ai_specific.note: This tool applies an AI model to hiring input. Several jurisdictions regulate that directly.
obligations: NYC Local Law 144: annual independent bias audit plus candidate notice for automated employment decision tools.
Illinois AI Video Interview Act: notice and consent when AI analyzes video interviews.
EU AI Act: employment-related AI is high-risk, with transparency and human-oversight duties.
Colorado SB 24-205: developer and deployer duties for high-risk AI in consequential decisions.
Across all of them the through-line is the same: disclose that AI is in the loop, keep a human decision-maker, and retain records.
